title: Arts example; power as necessity, wisdom as fate, love as harmony; Cap. 30 close
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): therefore we call ye influx belonging toward power necessity, belonging toward wisdom fate, belonging toward love harmony — plus what must be looks toward ye power belonging toward causes — plus what is ordered looks toward wisdom — plus because what is better looks toward love. then for ye sake belonging toward inhabitants — then for ye sake belonging toward ye house more aptly to be formed plus strengthened — then for its own sake — because for heavies it is better to be below plus for lights above — plus this at once results into harmony. plus so that at his own time also ye architect may need them — so that some may be light plus small, others great plus heavy — this truly also happens by fate from ye series belonging toward causes. because by necessity lights tend upward, heavies downward — light ones plus woods in ye roof — lest placed in ye roof they fall downward by their weight into ye house's ruin — for ye architect necessarily places heavier plus ampler stones in ye foundation. For we find ye same in arts.
pass_b_english: We find the same in the arts. For the architect necessarily sets the heavier and larger stones in the foundation, lest if placed in the roof they fall downward by their weight into the ruin of the house; the light ones and the timber he sets in the roof, because by necessity light things tend upward and heavy downward.

And this too happens by fate from the series of causes, that some things are light and small, others large and heavy, and that at the fitting time the architect needs them. And this at once results in harmony, because it is better for heavy things to be below and for light above — for their own sake, for the house more aptly formed and strengthened, and for the inhabitants' sake. And because what is better looks to love, what is ordered looks to wisdom, and what must be looks to the power of causes, therefore we call the influx of power necessity, of wisdom fate, of love harmony.
source_text: Idem in artibus invenimus. Nam architectus graviores amplioresque lapides necessario ponit in fundamento, ne in tecto positi pondere suo deorsum cadant in ruinam domus: leves et ligna in tecto, quia necessitate levia sursum, gravia deorsum tendunt. Hoc vero etiam fato fit ex causarum serie, ut alia sint levia et parva, alia grandia et gravia, et ut suo quoque tempore architectus iis indigat. Et hoc simul resultat in harmoniam, quia gravibus melius est esse infra, et levibus supra, tum gratia sui, tum gratia domus aptius formandae ac firmandae, tum gratia habitatorum. Et quia quod est melius respicit amor, et quod ordinatur respicit sapientia, et quod necesse est esse respicit potestas causarum, ideo influxum potestatis vocamus necessitatem, sapientiae fatum, amoris harmoniam.
